question: What is the primary reason for collecting family planning data in clinics?

options.A: Complying with international travel restrictions for nurses
options.B: Increasing the monthly salary of clinic nursing staff
options.C: Reducing the total number of patients visiting the facility
options.D: Forecasting contraceptive commodity needs and preventing stockouts

explanation: Reliable data allows health planners to predict consumption rates and supply enough commodities to prevent running out of family planning methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h1)

question: A clinic consistently fails to submit monthly family planning reports. What is the most likely consequence for that facility?

options.A: Automatic promotion of the head nurse to supervisor
options.B: Increased funding from international donor agencies
options.C: Frequent stockouts of contraceptive supplies and commodities
options.D: Immediate closure of the entire hospital facility

explanation: Supply chains depend on consumption reports to restock facilities, so missing data directly results in supply shortages. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h1)

question: Which tool is used for immediate, daily stroke-based counting of family planning clients during consultations?
explanation: Tally sheets provide a quick way to record services rendered in real time before transferring the totals to summary forms. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h2)

question: Why must nurses record client visits in the permanent register before completing the monthly summary?

options.A: Patients demand a written copy of the register page
options.B: The government requires two copies of every client fingerprint
options.C: The register serves as the primary source document for accurate aggregation
options.D: It speeds up the patient physical examination process

explanation: Summary forms rely on the detailed entries captured in the primary client register to ensure the numbers are verifiable. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h2)

question: Who is classified as a new acceptor in family planning registers?

options.A: A patient returning for a routine three-month pill refill
options.B: A client adopting a modern contraceptive method for the first time
options.C: A pregnant woman attending her first antenatal care visit
options.D: A client changing from injectable contraceptives to implants

explanation: New acceptors represent first-time users entering the modern family planning program within the reporting period. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h3)

question: A client stops taking oral contraceptive pills and immediately receives an intrauterine device. How should this client be recorded?
explanation: Switchers are clients who transition from one active contraceptive method to another without a gap in protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h3)

question: What is a frequent cause of errors when compiling monthly family planning reports?

options.A: Using blue ink instead of black ink in the register
options.B: Transposing digits when transferring tallies to summary sheets
options.C: Submitting the report two hours before the deadline
options.D: Allowing patients to fill out their own clinical charts

explanation: Mistakes often happen during manual transcription from daily logs to aggregated monthly report forms. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h4)

question: How can a nurse prevent the double-counting of client visits in monthly family planning reports?

options.A: Cross-checking daily tally sheets against individual entries in the client register
options.B: Destroying all tally sheets immediately after the morning shift
options.C: Reporting only the clients who pay cash for their services
options.D: Asking every patient to visit the clinic twice per week

explanation: Comparing source documents like registers with summary counts ensures each unique client visit is recorded only once. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h4)

question: What does the acronym NHMIS stand for in the Nigerian health care delivery system?

options.A: Nurses Housing and Medical Intervention Society

explanation: NHMIS is the official framework used across health facilities in Nigeria to collect and manage routine health data. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h5)

question: Why is strict adherence to monthly reporting deadlines important for the NHMIS process?

options.A: It prevents patients from requesting refunds for family planning services
options.B: It allows smooth integration of facility data into state and national databases
options.C: It stops the printing press from producing more register books
options.D: It guarantees that nurses receive holiday allowances from the federal government

explanation: Timely submission prevents missing data in higher-level aggregates, keeping national health dashboards current. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h5)

question: How can a nurse manager use monthly family planning data to improve local clinic services?

options.A: By closing the family planning unit during peak harvest seasons
options.B: By reducing the number of working hours for all clinic personnel
options.C: By increasing the consultation fees for high-demand services
options.D: By identifying popular contraceptive methods and adjusting future supply orders

explanation: Analyzing local consumption trends helps nurses request the right quantities and types of commodities for their specific patient population. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h6)

question: Clinic records reveal a sudden drop in return visits for injectable contraceptives. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Stop ordering injectable contraceptives from the local government store
options.B: Investigate possible client barriers and schedule community outreach tracking
options.C: Ignore the data because monthly summaries are only meant for headquarters
options.D: Assume all missing clients have permanently relocated to another country

explanation: Using local data to spot negative trends prompts proactive nursing interventions like follow-up visits or community mobilization. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h6)
